facts.content: Patient reports 3 days of watery diarrhea affecting activities of daily living.
facts.source_text: CC: 3 days watery diarrhea affecting ADLs; needs proximity to toilet

facts.content: Patient has watery and loose stools approximately 6-7 times per day without blood.
facts.source_text: Stool ~6–7/day; watery/loose; no blood

facts.content: Patient experiences crampy intermittent pain in the left lower quadrant of the abdomen.
facts.source_text: LLQ crampy, intermittent abdominal pain; non-radiating

facts.content: Initial vomiting at onset, now resolved.
facts.source_text: Initial vomiting at onset; now resolved

facts.content: Felt febrile at onset, but currently no fever; feels weak and shaky.
facts.source_text: Felt febrile at onset; no current fever; feels weak/shaky

facts.content: Appetite is reduced but tolerating fluids; eating soups and smoothies.
facts.source_text: ↓ appetite; tolerating fluids; eating soups/smoothies

facts.content: Possible trigger is Chinese takeaway eaten 4 days ago.
facts.source_text: Possible trigger: Chinese takeaway 4 days ago (ate at Chinese restaurant)

facts.content: Had contact with a sick child who vomited; no diarrhea in the household.
facts.source_text: Sick contact: child vomited; no diarrhea in household

facts.content: Patient has well-controlled asthma.
facts.source_text: PMH: Asthma (well controlled)

facts.content: Patient uses an inhaler.
facts.source_text: Meds: Inhaler

facts.content: Patient is an accountant working despite symptoms.
facts.source_text: Accountant; working despite symptoms

facts.content: Patient lives with wife and two kids.
facts.source_text: lives with wife + 2 kids

facts.content: Patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol.
facts.source_text: non-smoker; no etOH

facts.content: Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral or foodborne, with 3 days of watery diarrhea and left lower quadrant crampy pain.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral/foodborne: 3 days watery diarrhea, LLQ crampy pain, initial vomiting/subjective fever; no blood in stool; maintaining PO fluids; clinically mild without red flags.

facts.content: Asthma is stable on inhaler.
facts.source_text: 2) Asthma—stable on inhaler.

facts.content: Encourage oral rehydration with fluids and ORS as needed.
facts.source_text: Oral rehydration: encourage fluids; ORS (e.g., Dioralyte) as needed

facts.content: Advise small frequent bland meals, advancing diet as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Diet: small frequent bland meals; advance as tolerated

facts.content: Use paracetamol, two tablets up to four times a day as needed for pain or fever.
facts.source_text: Antipyretic/analgesic: paracetamol 2 tabs up to QID PRN

facts.content: Recommend rest; patient off work for 2-3 days.
facts.source_text: Rest; off work 2–3 days

facts.content: Safety-net advice to return if not improving in 3-4 days, or if symptoms worsen.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: return if not improving in 3–4 days → consider stool studies

facts.content: Seek urgent care if there is blood in stool, persistent or high fever, severe or worsening abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or inability to keep fluids down.
facts.source_text: Urgent care if blood in stool, persistent/high fever, severe/worsening abdo pain, signs of dehydration (oliguria, dizziness), inability to keep fluids down

facts.content: Continue inhaler as prescribed with no change.
facts.source_text: Continue inhaler as prescribed; no change
